title: 2024 budget review and tax rate reductions
subtitle: Elora BIA loan, termite funding, capital project shifts, councillor pay phase-in, fees by-law and urban forestry update.
overview: Over two days the Committee of the Whole worked through the 2024 draft budget. The draft began with a 8.54% tax increase. After the committee's changes, the treasurer reported the rate at 7.38%. The committee recommended Council approve the 2024 budget as amended {{vote:m17}}.

Main recommendations: using OLG funds for the termite management program {{vote:m2}}, raising investment income {{vote:m5}} and trimming the transfer to the capital reserve for asset management {{vote:m6}}. It also recommended removing the rented temporary washrooms in downtown Elora, with staff to look for other funding {{vote:m10}}, and phasing in the Council salary increase over 2024 and 2025 {{vote:m12}}. Some capital projects were swapped between years {{vote:m4}}. The committee recommended a $50,000 interest-free loan to the Elora BIA {{vote:m14}} and a 2024 fees and charges by-law {{vote:m9}}.

The committee also received the urban forestry update for information {{vote:m1}}. It asked for tennis to be included in the Parks and Recreation Master Plan, and for staff to look at the Fergus Grand Theatre's profitability and at working with the Elora Centre for the Arts. The Mayor and a councillor stepped out for items where they declared conflicts of interest. Council makes the final decisions.

decisions.detail: The committee recommended Council approve the 2024 budget as amended during the two days of deliberations {{vote:m17}}.
The committee recommended directing the OLG funds allocated to Economic Development in 2024 to the termite management program {{vote:m2}}.

The committee recommended delaying the Tourism Office renovation and Elora tourism washroom design to 2025 and moving Sportsplex Pad B seating heating and Sportsplex Hall basketball nets into 2024 {{vote:m4}}.
The committee recommended reducing the 2024 transfer to the General Capital reserve for asset management by $50,000 {{vote:m6}}.
The committee recommended removing the rental of temporary downtown Elora washrooms from the 2024 budget and directing staff to look for other funding {{vote:m10}}.
The committee recommended directing staff to phase in the salary increase for Members of Council over 2024 and 2025 {{vote:m12}}.
The committee recommended an interest-free loan of $50,000 to the Elora BIA {{vote:m14}}.
The committee recommended a by-law setting 2024 fees and charges and repealing by-laws 2023-01, 2023-06 and 2023-29 {{vote:m9}}.

debate: Staff said the draft was above the combined Township index because of insurance, benefits and gravel-road material cost pressures. They warned that cutting committed service levels or the asset management transfer would have longer-term effects. Staff suggested making up the asset management reduction in a later budget.

Councillors questioned cutting the gravel maintenance budget, citing rural residents' limited services. Staff said it would mean about six fewer lane kilometres of gravel. That reduction was not pursued, nor were cuts to staff learning and development or beautification.
Staff cautioned against raising revenue budgets, such as investment income and committee of adjustment fees, because falling interest rates or fewer applications would later push costs onto taxes.

On capital items, councillors weighed deferring tourism renovations against bringing forward basketball nets and heated seating. Staff said the nets needed engineering work, and portable nets could be bought sooner.

Delegates from both BIAs described private garbage collection costs as crippling and asked for continued township support. The Elora BIA tied its loan request to replacing aging hydro-pole Christmas lights.
